title: Tire Pressure Monitoring System: Overview
introduction: The tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) passes pressure information from the wheels to the vehicle's electronics, then brings a problem to your attention through the instruments. I follow that handoff like a relay race: the sensor's radio message is only the opening leg. This overview explains the route and the reasons for a warning; pressure specifications, warning-pattern interpretation and diagnostic tests are outside its scope.

edits.text: From Tire Sensors to Dashboard Warnings

The BCM (body control module) monitors tire pressure using battery-operated sensors mounted to the valve stems. Each sensor transmits tire-pressure information by radio to the RTM (radio transceiver module). The RTM passes that information to the BCM over a LIN (local interconnect network). When tire pressure falls below the low-pressure limit, or a fault is present, the IPC (instrument panel cluster) illuminates the TPMS warning indicator and the message center displays a message.
edits.why: The communication route explains how information leaves the rotating wheel and reaches the vehicle's control electronics. I keep the warning's meaning separate from its appearance: this overview identifies both low pressure and a fault as reasons for an alert, so the indicator alone does not establish which condition is present.
